findings.claim: The summary left out handoffs, one part of the design. How it works now names them.

verdict.text: How it works now says that handoffs in `.okf/handoffs/` carry where work stopped into the next session, that `/handoff` writes one and `/continue` reads it back, and it cites ADR 0008.
The sentence matches the ADR and both skills.
Where it stands no longer names the in-flight nudge ticket and now says only that work in flight lives as loop tickets in `.loop/`, which is true.
Row r4 still holds and the stamp is green, so the verdict is pass.
Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree myself.
Rows r2, r3 and r5 passed, and so did the other gates.
The summary body is 499 words, under the 500 limit.
The new sentence against ADR 0008: the ADR says /handoff writes a concept in `.okf/handoffs/` through kmctl, and /continue lists the live handoffs and loads the ones the user picks.
`apm/.apm/skills/handoff/SKILL.md` says a handoff is "a concept in `.okf/handoffs/`" so `/continue` can find it.
`apm/.apm/skills/continue/SKILL.md` says it resumes "from earlier /handoff notes in .okf/handoffs/".
"Reads it back" is a fair short form of list, pick and load.
r4 (judgment): I read the round diff in `.okf/summary.md`.
The "OKF as it is" bullet was reworded to fit the word limit, and it keeps the same claims: two named extensions, `handoff_key` and `checked`, and no `covers` field.
ADR 0008 still appears with ADR 0001 and ADR 0022 as evidence that verbs write front matter, so no section has become a list of single-decision links.
Every part of the design is now named: the CLI, the APM package, the Action, the template, the layered reads and handoffs.
The new Where it stands line makes no claim that will go stale.
